title: Compound frequency × severity
about: The smallest model: an uncertain number of incidents per year, each costing a lognormal amount. Move the rate and the cost and watch the tail.

title: Phishing filter (period-scoped probability)
about: 600 emails a period meet a filter whose block rate is uncertain and drawn once per period. The spread of the total comes from the bad periods, which a per-event draw would hide.

title: Intrusion: detection, then a sequential response
about: An attack is detected with a probability; an undetected attack gets no response and runs to a breach that costs more for the dwell time. A detected one is tried in order: contained with an uncertain rate, else escalated, else lost despite the response. Lower the detection rate and watch the liability category take over the tail.

knobs.label: Breach cost when undetected, most likely

title: Machine repair (holding times and a cap)
about: Failures take days to repair; downtime cost accrues per day and the parts bill is capped. Values can land in the period after the failure.

knobs.label: Downtime cost per day, most likely

title: Pump station (the reference model)
about: Wear trips and grid outages merge at a fault check; sequential outcomes, holding times in hours and days, a per-day production cost and a chained inspection.

title: Two pumps from one template
about: A repair path defined once and instanced for two pumps, both wired to shared replacement and recommissioning nodes; the second instance overrides the replacement probability.

title: Frequent minor faults and rare critical failures
about: Two regimes in one plant: a stream of minor faults, each a repair bill, and a critical failure a few times a decade costing a hundred times more. The period total has two peaks, the years with only minor faults and the years with a failure; the log-scaled histogram shows both, the linear one shows how the rare regime dominates the range.

knobs.label: Minor faults per year, most likely
Critical failures per year, most likely

title: A register of a hundred risks
about: A hundred risks, each an event rate and a loss per event, with a control that stops a share of events and a cap on any one loss. The exceedance curve of the period total is the cumulative risk profile; the breakdown by source ranks the risks. Every rate is a gamma, so the exact distribution is closed form in the rate and the curve comes with bounds, though a hundred lognormals take the transform about a minute here.

knobs.label: Share of events the control stops

title: Cooling plant as a reliability block diagram
about: Chillers two of three, pumps one of two and a control system in series, each with a mean time between failures and a mean repair time in hours. The engine simulates the units' failures and repairs as a Markov chain and fires the outage each time the plant goes down, so a redundant block's failures cluster as they do in life; the stationary rate, system MTBF and unavailability are shown beside the results. Each outage costs a callout and production per day for as long as the plant is down: the holding is the outage itself, the time the chain takes to bring the plant back.

knobs.label: Lost production per day, most likely

title: Counts that are not Poisson: every n-th pallet, and a press under repair
about: Two sources with their own clocks. A filter is changed after every n-th pallet, so its count per year is the pallet count divided by n with far less spread than Poisson; try the log-scale histogram with a small n. A press that has failed cannot fail again until repaired: after each failure the source is silent for the repair, and its long-run rate is one over the mean time to failure plus the mean repair. The plan sizes both from their exact means; the press's spread is estimated from the run.

knobs.label: Press failures per year while running

title: A common shock: risks that rise and fall together
about: Three cyber risks, two of them scaled by one threat climate drawn once per year and shared, so a bad year is bad for both at once. Widen the climate's spread and watch the exceedance tail thicken while every mean stays put; bring its 90th percentile down to 1.05 for near-independence. Pin that as the baseline and compare.

knobs.label: Phishing incidents per year, most likely
Malware incidents per year, most likely

title: Rates that vary by period: a storm season
about: Monthly periods. Storm claims follow a twelve-value cycle peaking in late summer, burst pipes one peaking in winter, theft none: period p takes the multiplier at p modulo twelve. Tick the series to see the cycle in the totals; the exact mean, variance and distribution describe a month taken at random from the cycle, which is what a run over whole years sees.

title: An eight-hour shift as the period
about: Jobs arrive at a truncated-normal rate per shift; the labour rate is drawn once per shift and shared by every job in it (scope: period), so the shift's cost moves together; a breakdown brings a callout PERT with a flatter shape than the default and a truncated lognormal for parts. The histogram's width comes from the shared rate as much as from the count.

knobs.label: Labour rate per job, most likely

title: Observed data as the model
about: The claim severity is the empirical distribution of a hundred and twenty past claims, resampled as they were; the claim class is a categorical with the handling cost of each class. Resampling observed data says what has happened; a fitted family says what could, which is why the tail of this histogram stops where the data does.

title: Heavy tails, a cap, and layers of the total
about: Three heavy-tailed severities: a Pareto with a finite variance, a fatter Pareto held by an insurance limit (cap), and a generalised Pareto. Two layers of the period total report what is retained under an aggregate deductible and what a reinsurance layer above it pays; with the exact distribution their means come with bounds. Lower the open Pareto's alpha below two and its variance is infinite: the exact method declines, and the cap is what makes the other tail computable.

title: Two sites in one model, with the run's criteria set in the file
about: Two graphs, north and south, their categories added across both. Each site loses production per hour of outage and pays a callout; the north's repair is a Weibull, the south's exponential. The file sets the run's criteria: more hits on every outcome, a looser error on the means, a deeper tail, a cap on the periods, and the series kept for a plot. Exponential, uniform, log-uniform, triangular and Weibull families.

knobs.label: North repair, Weibull scale in hours

title: Discrete values: damaged items, resends, inspections, complaints
about: A shipment of items arrives and each item is damaged with a probability, so the damaged count is binomial and booked as items; a damaged shipment needs a geometric number of resends before it is accepted; whether a shipment is inspected is a Bernoulli; the complaints it draws are negative binomial. Pick the items or complaints category to see a count distribution rather than a money one.

knobs.label: Probability a shipment needs a resend
